t: Section 1941(b) of the Social Security Act (42 U.S.C. 1396w–1(b)) is amended in paragraph (3)(A) by striking “$2,387,000,000” and inserting “$1,960,000,000”.

fable.w: This section only changes a dollar amount in an existing Social Security Act provision. There is no tempting participation reading: it has no comment period, rulemaking, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outside parties, or right to sue. No party outside the federal government is involved in any federal decision.
fable.s: is amended in paragraph (3)(A) by striking “$2,387,000,000” and inserting “$1,960,000,000”

qwen_block.w: This section is a technical amendment to a statutory dollar amount. It does not involve any consultation, coordination, or interaction with parties outside the federal government. It is purely a legislative adjustment of funding levels.
qwen_block.s: Section 1941(b) of the Social Security Act (42 U.S.C. 1396w–1(b)) is amended in paragraph (3)(A) by striking “$2,387,000,000” and inserting “$1,960,000,000”.

opus.w: This section only replaces one dollar amount with another in section 1941(b)(3)(A) of the Social Security Act. It sets up no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking or right to sue. The fact that it amends the Social Security Act does not bring any outside party into a federal decision.
opus.b: 1. **Reasoning.** It might be tempting to read this as participation because it amends the Social Security Act, which covers programs involving States. But the provision only lowers a dollar figure in section 1941(b)(3)(A). It sets up no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking or right to sue, so no one outside the federal government takes part in any decision.

qwen_chat.w: This section is a simple appropriation amendment that changes a specific dollar amount in the Social Security Act. It does not establish any process for consulting with, coordinating with, or receiving input from parties outside the federal government. There are no advisory committees, public hearings, comment periods, or consultation requirements mentioned.
qwen_chat.s: Section 1941(b) of the Social Security Act (42 U.S.C. 1396w–1(b)) is amended in paragraph (3)(A) by striking “$2,387,000,000” and inserting “$1,960,000,000”.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that changing a funding cap affects who gets benefits, and thus indirectly involves the public. However, the text itself contains no mechanism for public input, consultation, or participation. It is a purely internal legislative amendment to a dollar figure.
